clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 3. The emitter source between v0.16.5 and v0.16.7 and which changes reach instructions of the deployed PoolManager, including shift_literal_by_non_literal at 6 PoolManager sites (TickBitmap.sol:72, :96, :110, BitMath.sol:21-22, :40-42) and the touch_memory skip of the bound check for a non-literal offset already checked in the block.
clearedSpotChecks.note: I fetched https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/vm/compiler/ir/x86/emitter.cpp (8,539 lines) and read shift_literal_by_non_literal at lines 5253-5325 and the touch_memory skip at lines 6301-6311. I rebuilt the window arithmetic in Python from that text: SHL table add96({7,0,0,0}, 0, value) with the window at +64, carry load at -1 byte, per-qword vpsllq by b then vpsrlq by 8; SHR and SAR table add96(value, fill, {fill0, fill1, 7, 0}) with the mask at +80, carry load at +1 byte. For SHL, SHR and SAR, 206 values (0, 1, 2^255, 2^255+1, 2^256-2, 2^256-1 and 200 random words) and every count 0 to 259 plus 2^64 and 2^256-1 (clamped to 256 as destructive_mov_stack_elem_to_bounded_rax(shift, 256) does) give 0 differences from the EVM specification. So the 6 PoolManager sites compute the same mask and bit positions in TickBitmap.flipTick, nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord and BitMath as on Ethereum. The touch_memory skip at 6302 needs the same stack element to have passed is_bounded_by_bits and the memory growth with at least read_size earlier in the block; memory does not shrink inside a frame, so the skipped check would pass. The deployed code at 0x188d586ddcf52439676ca21a244753fa19f9ea8e read with eth_getCode from https://rpc.monad.xyz is 24,009 bytes and equal byte for byte to the harness input monad-pm-runtime.hex (sha256 prefix 288b97729c9e4f34, as in networks.json).

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 4, edges and unexecuted shapes. The two mul_mod2 MULMOD sites (pc 22378 with literal modulus 2^128 in FullMath.mulDiv called from Position.update, pc 22639 with literal modulus 2^96) are evidenced by micro programs; on a correct node the 2^128 site ends in a revert at Pool.sol:192 and the 2^96 site gives an amount of at least 2^160 that loses the comparison in SwapMath or reverts in a cast.
clearedSpotChecks.note: Disassembly of the on-chain bytecode shows pc 22378 is PUSH17 2^128 SWAP2 MULMOD and pc 22639 is PUSH13 2^96 SWAP2 MULMOD, each right after the require(denominator > prod1) jump to 0x0330 and the prod1 == 0 branch, which is the remainder := mulmod(a, b, denominator) of the 512-bit branch at src/libraries/FullMath.sol:47-49. That branch runs only when a*b >= 2^256, so the quotient is at least 2^256/2^128 = 2^128 at the first site; Position.update returns it as feesOwed (src/libraries/Position.sol:92-96) and Pool.modifyLiquidity casts it with toInt128 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:192), which reverts for x >= 2^127 (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:56-58). At the second site the quotient is at least 2^160, which on the swap path either fails the amountRemainingLessFee >= amountIn or uint256(amountRemaining) >= amountOut comparison (src/libraries/SwapMath.sol:68, :90) or is cast later. The other MULMOD sites with 2^96 operands (for example pc 20958, the round-up mulmod of src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:252 that runs on every getAmount1Delta) take the runtime call shape per shapes/pm-shapes.json, which the interpreter shares and the 2,007 mined transactions matched. I did not rerun the micro programs; the clearance of the mul_mod2 arms rests on the stored micro outputs (micro/out-v167.txt) and the fault injections f4 and f5 that showed those programs detect a wrong bit width.

clearedSpotChecks.check: Task 2. 2,007 mined Monad PoolManager transactions replayed through Monad's interpreter and native emitter at v0.16.7 and v0.16.5 with MIP-8 page gas, 0 differences between engines and every frame status, return value and log equal to the block.
clearedSpotChecks.note: web3_clientVersion on https://rpc.monad.xyz, https://rpc1.monad.xyz and https://rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com returned Monad/0.16.7 today, so the release replayed is the one the public endpoints run. https://docs.monad.xyz/developer-essentials/gas-pricing.md states that the gas charged is the gas limit, which explains the 76 top-level frames whose reported gasUsed is the whole limit; that rule changes no return data. page_tracker.hpp at v0.16.7 (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/category-labs/monad@v0.16.7/category/execution/ethereum/state3/page_tracker.hpp, 106 lines) holds per-page accessed and dirty state as the replay models. The remaining gas residuals are multiples of cold-access costs set by other contracts in the same transaction; src/ never reads gasleft to decide an amount, so they cannot change a computed value. A replay is limited to the paths users already took; the scenario batteries and micro programs cover the rest. I did not re-run replay.cpp.
